questions.text: Amount of zakat cannot be used in _____ .
questions.explanation: Fixed: the classic CSS key (also CSS Times 2005 compilation) is "Mosque"; Zakat requires tamleek (transfer of ownership to an eligible person), so it cannot fund mosque construction. Original options vary between sources. Low confidence: with strict Hanafi tamleek, none of these buildings can be funded directly from Zakat (cssprep keys "All of these"), but the original FPSC paper offered only Madrasah/Mosque/Hospital and the accepted answer is Mosque. Zakat can reach a madrasah through its eligible students and a hospital through poor patients. Source: CSS 2005 Islamiat past paper (cssprep.com.pk); key checked against the CSS Times 2005–2016 solved compilation.

questions.text: What is the primary role of Bait-ul-Mal in the Islamic economic system?

options.A: To serve as a treasury for social welfare and public assistance
options.B: To regulate trade and commerce in the Islamic state
options.C: To collect and distribute Zakat only
options.D: To manage the personal wealth of the Caliph

questions.explanation: The primary role of Bait-ul-Mal is to serve as a treasury for social welfare and public assistance in the Islamic economic system. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, economic system.

questions.text: After performing the obligatory prayers, what is the status of seeking lawful (halal) earning in Islam?
questions.explanation: Seeking lawful (halal) earning after performing the obligatory prayers is Farz (Obligatory) in Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, economic system.

questions.text: What are Usher and Khums in the context of Islamic teachings?

options.A: Two kinds of Tax in Islam

questions.explanation: Usher and Khums are two kinds of Tax in Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, economic system.

questions.text: Which type of tax is traditionally levied on agricultural lands in Islamic history?
questions.explanation: The tax traditionally levied on agricultural lands in Islamic history is Kharaj. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, economic system.

questions.text: What does the term 'Ghermeen' refer to in Islamic financial terminology?
questions.explanation: In Islamic financial terminology, 'Ghermeen' refers to debtors — individuals who are in debt and eligible to receive Zakat. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, economic system.

questions.text: Who is the author of the Islamic book 'Kitab al Amwal' which focuses on Islamic revenue and finance?

options.A: Abu Ubaid al Qasim Ibn Sallam

questions.explanation: The book 'Kitab al Amwal' was authored by Abu Ubaid al Qasim Ibn Sallam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, economic system.

questions.text: In which year did Imam Ghazali pass away according to the Hijri calendar?
questions.explanation: Imam Ghazali passed away in 505 Hijri according to the Hijri calendar. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, famous jurists (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who were the notable pupils of Imam Abu Hanifa?

options.B: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Imam Bukhari
options.C: Both Imam Yusuf and Imam Muhammad

questions.explanation: The most notable pupils of Imam Abu Hanifa were Imam Abu Yusuf and Imam Muhammad al-Shaybani. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, famous jurists (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which book was written by Imam Ghazali?
questions.explanation: Imam Ghazali wrote Ihya Ulum al-Din (The Revival of Religious Sciences), his magnum opus covering Islamic spirituality, jurisprudence, and ethics. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, famous jurists (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What was the real name of Ibn Taymiyyah?
questions.explanation: The real name of Ibn Taymiyyah was Taqi-ud-din Ahmad ibn Abd al-Halim. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, famous jurists (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: In which year did the author of Tahzeeb ul Ahkam, a significant Islamic text, pass away?
questions.explanation: The author of Tahzeeb ul Ahkam, Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Tusi (also known as Sheikh al-Ta'ifa), passed away in 460 Hijri. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, famous jurists.

questions.text: At what age did Imam Shafi memorize the Quran?
questions.explanation: Imam Shafi memorized the Holy Quran at the age of seven. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, famous jurists.

questions.text: Which prominent Islamic scholar died in the same year Imam Shafi (RA) was born?
questions.explanation: Imam Abu Hanifa (RA), the founder of the Hanafi school of thought, passed away in 150 AH — the very same year Imam Shafi (RA) was born. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, famous jurists.

questions.text: Writer of Al Kafi Muhammad bin Yaqub Al Kuliyani died in _?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Yaqub Al Kulayni, the compiler of Al-Kafi, died in 329 Hijri (941 CE). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fiqh jafria (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Who is the author of the famous Islamic book 'Al-Kafi'?

options.A: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq

questions.explanation: The famous Islamic book 'Al-Kafi' was authored by Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, also known as Sheikh Al-Kulayni. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fiqh jafria.

questions.text: What is the name of the author of Tahdhib al-Ahkam fi Sharh al-Din al-Mut'ah?

options.A: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Tusi
options.B: Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Husayn al-Musawi

questions.explanation: The author of Tahdhib al-Ahkam fi Sharh al-Din al-Mut'ah is Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Tusi, known as Shaykh al-Ta'ifah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, fiqh jafria.

questions.text: What does the term 'Qazf' refer to in Islamic law?
questions.explanation: In Islamic law, 'Qazf' refers to the false accusation of Zina (adultery/fornication) against a chaste person without producing the required witnesses. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, islamic criminal law hudood.

questions.text: Which tribe did the woman accused of theft during the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) era belong to?
questions.explanation: The woman accused of theft during the Prophet's (PBUH) era belonged to the tribe of Banu Makhzum. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, islamic criminal law hudood.

questions.text: What is the punishment prescribed by Shariah for a married adulterer?
questions.explanation: The punishment prescribed by Shariah for a married adulterer (muhsan) is Rajm (Stoning to death). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, islamic criminal law hudood.

questions.text: Who are the rightful recipients of Diyat according to Islamic law?
questions.explanation: According to Islamic law, the rightful recipients of Diyat (blood money) are the heirs of the victim. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, islamic criminal law hudood.

questions.text: What does the term 'Arsh' refer to in Islamic jurisprudence?

options.A: Compensation paid to the victim or his heirs

questions.explanation: In Islamic jurisprudence, 'Arsh' refers to compensation paid to the victim or his heirs for bodily injury or harm where exact Qisas is not applicable. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, islamic criminal law hudood.

questions.text: Who wrote the book 'Usool-e-Dawat'?
questions.explanation: The book 'Usool-e-Dawat' was written by Dr. Abdul Karim Zaidan. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic law jurisprudence (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which term in Islamic jurisprudence refers to actions that are neither rewarded nor sinful if not performed?
questions.explanation: The term for actions that are neither rewarded nor sinful if performed or omitted is Mubah. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic law jurisprudence.

questions.text: What is the share of a husband in inheritance if there are no entitled descendants (children/grandchildren)?
questions.explanation: Fixed: Surah An-Nisa 4:12 — the husband gets 1/2 if the wife leaves no children, and 1/4 if she does. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic law jurisprudence.

questions.text: What does the term 'Qalala' refer to in Islamic inheritance law?

options.A: A person with no surviving parents or children
options.B: A person who leaves behind only female heirs
options.C: A deceased person who had no spouse at the time of death
options.D: A person who dies without leaving any will

questions.explanation: In Islamic inheritance law, 'Qalala' refers to a person with no surviving parents or children. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic law jurisprudence.

questions.text: What is the term used in Islamic jurisprudence for the wealth or property left by a deceased person?
questions.explanation: The term used in Islamic jurisprudence for the wealth or property left by a deceased person is Taraka. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, miscellaneous islamic law jurisprudence.

questions.text: What is the minimum number of members required for the Council of Islamic Ideology?
questions.explanation: The minimum number of members required for the Council of Islamic Ideology is 8. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, political system.

questions.text: The concept of 'Istihsan' in Islamic jurisprudence is primarily attributed to which Islamic scholar?
questions.explanation: The concept of 'Istihsan' (juristic preference) in Islamic jurisprudence is primarily attributed to Imam Abu Hanifa. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which of the following is not recognized as one of the four Imams of the Sunni schools of jurisprudence?
questions.explanation: Imam Jaffer Sadiq (R.A) is not among the four Imams of Sunni schools; the four are Imam Abu Hanifa, Imam Malik, Imam Shafi, and Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (R.A). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: What is the status of a marriage contract in Hanafi jurisprudence if it is concluded without the presence of witnesses?
questions.explanation: In Hanafi jurisprudence, a marriage contract concluded without the presence of witnesses is invalid. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: What was the original name of the Islamic scholar known as Imam Shafi (RA)?
questions.explanation: The original name of Imam Shafi (RA) was Muhammad bin Idrees. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: What do the terms Hanfi, Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali refer to in Islamic studies?
questions.explanation: Hanfi, Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali refer to the four major Sunni Fiqhi doctrines (schools of Islamic jurisprudence). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: What is the term used in Islamic jurisprudence for an act that is discouraged but not sinful to perform?
questions.explanation: The term for an act that is discouraged but not sinful in Islamic jurisprudence is Makruh-i-Tanzihi. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: Which Islamic school of thought is known for emphasizing rationalism in understanding the divine commands?
questions.explanation: Mutazilism is the Islamic school of thought known for emphasizing rationalism in understanding divine commands. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: Who is recognized as the founder of the Hanafi School of Islamic jurisprudence?
questions.explanation: The Hanafi School of Islamic jurisprudence was founded by Imam Abu Hanifa (Nu'man ibn Thabit). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: According to the Hanafi School of Islamic Law, how many total sharers are recognized in the Law of Inheritance?
questions.explanation: According to the Hanafi School of Islamic Law, 12 total sharers are recognized in the Law of Inheritance. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: Is Witr prayer considered obligatory (Fard) in Islam?
questions.explanation: Witr prayer is not Fard; according to the Hanafi school, it is Wajib (necessary/obligatory). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, schools of thought.

questions.text: In Arabic, what word is used to refer to a neighbor?
questions.explanation: The Arabic word for a neighbor is Jār. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, social system.

questions.text: Which fundamental right emphasizes the sacredness of life in Islam?
questions.explanation: The Right to live is the fundamental right in Islam that emphasizes the sacredness and sanctity of human life. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, social system.

questions.text: What is the literal meaning of the Islamic term 'Qiyas'?
questions.explanation: The literal meaning of the Islamic term 'Qiyas' is to assess. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, sources of islamic law.

questions.text: What does the term 'Ijma' refer to in Islamic jurisprudence?
questions.explanation: Ijma refers to the consensus of Muslim jurists on a particular legal issue in Islamic jurisprudence. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, sources of islamic law.

questions.text: What is considered the second primary source of Islamic jurisprudence after the Quran?
questions.explanation: The second primary source of Islamic jurisprudence after the Quran is Hadith (Sunnah). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, sources of islamic law.

questions.text: What is the third source of Islamic law called?
questions.explanation: The third source of Islamic law is Ijma (consensus of the Muslim jurists). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, sources of islamic law.

questions.text: What is the position of Sunnah in the hierarchy of Islamic sources of guidance?
questions.explanation: Sunnah holds the second position in the hierarchy of Islamic sources of guidance, coming after the Holy Quran. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, sources of islamic law.

questions.text: What portion of a treasure found by Muslims is due as Khums according to Islamic law?
questions.explanation: According to Islamic law, one fifth of a treasure (Rikaz) found by Muslims is due as Khums. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, sources of islamic law.

questions.text: According to Islamic economic principles, what is the term for the mandatory charitable giving of wealth to help the less fortunate?
questions.explanation: The mandatory charitable giving of wealth to help the less fortunate in Islam is called Zakat. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, zakat.

questions.text: To whom is Zakat primarily distributed according to Islamic teachings?

options.B: Those employed to collect Zakat and those whose hearts are to be reconciled
options.C: Debtors, wayfarers, and for the cause of Allah

questions.explanation: Zakat is primarily distributed to eight categories of recipients as mentioned in Surah Al-Tawbah (9:60), so "All of these" is correct. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, zakat.

questions.text: Zakat, one of the Five Pillars of Islam, is considered a type of what kind of worship?
questions.explanation: Zakat is a financial worship (Ibadah Maliyyah) that involves giving a fixed portion of one's wealth to the deserving. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, zakat.

questions.text: What portion of the harvest's value is given as Zakat on land irrigated through labor-intensive means?
questions.explanation: The Zakat on land irrigated through labor-intensive means (such as wells, buckets, or manual watering) is one-twentieth (1/20 or 5%) of the harvest. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, zakat.

questions.text: When were the orders of Zakat first given in Islam?
questions.explanation: The orders of Zakat were first given in Islam in 2 A.H. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, zakat.
